Milt Hinton is the “Dean of Jazz Bassists” and a true living legend in American music. Milt’s career started in Chicago in the era of Al Capone and included work with virtually every major jazz artist, including Cab Calloway, Louis Armstrong, Count Basie, Hank Jones and Joe Williams. After years on the road he became part of the “New York Rhythm Section” and recorded constantly with countless jazz and popular music artists. It has been estimated that Milt has performed on 500 jazz albums and an equal number in the pop field. His photographs of fellow jazz musicians have been shown in exhibits across the country and can be seen in his books Bass Line and Over Time. Today Milt is still in demand in the studios, colleges and at jazz festivals around the world.
He and his wife Mona can be seen in the movie “A Great Day in Harlem.”
Milt was interviewed by jazz vocalist and friend Joe Williams on May 31, 1995 aboard a cruise ship in the Caribbean.

MR: Greetings. My name is Monk Rowe of the Hamilton College Music Department. We are filming for our jazz archive today and as a very special event, we have two of the jazz greats with us this afternoon, Mr. Milt Hinton, bassist extraordinaire, and the great jazz vocalist Joe Williams. And we’re going to let them talk, and relate some of their experiences in the world of jazz.
